ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the figure, point D is on side AB of $\triangle ABC$, with $\angle ABC = \angle ACD$. $\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ACD$; if $AD = 2$ and $AB = 8$, find the length of $AC$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\triangle ABC\sim \triangle ACD$,\\
it follows that $\frac{AC}{AD}=\frac{AB}{AC}$,\\
Given $AD=2$, $AB=8$,\\
we have $\frac{AC}{2}=\frac{8}{AC}$,\\
therefore $AC= \boxed{4}$.

method.method_draft: Read from the image that triangles ABC and ACD have bases AB and AD on the same straight line AB, so they share the same altitude from C to line AB. Thus their area ratio is [ABC]/[ACD] = AB/AD = 8/2 = 4. From the stated similarity triangle ABC ~ triangle ACD, the linear scale factor from triangle ACD to triangle ABC is AB/AC, because AB in the larger triangle corresponds to AC in the smaller triangle.
